newsitem.title: USA: Labor Secretary Reich -- US wage growth slowing - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Labor Secretary Reich -- US wage growth slowing - RFTV.

text.p: The growth of wages seems to be slowing and that should help allay concerns on Wall Street about wage-push inflation, Labor Secretary Robert Reich said.
"There does appear to be a slowdown," he told Reuters Financial Television on Friday. "There are still wage gains going on ... but not quite as fast as we were seeing before."
He pointed to news this week that average hourly earnings held steady in October and that growth of employers' costs slowed in the third quarter.
Reich said that the 50-cent-per-hour increase in the minimum wage that took place on October 1 looks to have had a negligible effect on both overall wages and employment.
"What we are seeing and what we will continue to see is a negligible effect, both with regard to total employment and also with regards to wages," he said.

He called the labor markets "fairly tight" and said that was forcing employers to improve the skills of their existing workers through training and take on new employees from the inner cities who in the past may have been overlooked.
He said he did not know whether the jobless rate has bottomed out. The unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October. It fell as low as 5.1 percent in August.
"I don't know whether we've bottomed out," Reich said, in response to a question.
